title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an AI scribe transcribe her first urologist appointment in Australia. The tool falsely added to her medical record that she micro-dosed psychedelic mushrooms, which she has never done. She discovered the error after kidney stone surgery in March when a post-operative letter to her GP said mushroom use could explain earlier bleeding around her kidneys. Ms Green, who was receiving workers' compensation, feared the false drug claim could hurt her case. After she complained, the urologist apologised, corrected the letter, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice.

The incident highlights wider concerns about AI scribes in healthcare. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates 40 per cent of GPs regularly use them, but a Digital Rights Watch report found errors such as recording the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis or inventing epilepsy. The Therapeutic Goods Administration is reviewing AI scribes and will release findings in coming weeks, with breaches to be acted upon. Ms Green would only consent to AI again with a doctor she already trusts.
